60074615.s: Modon Lake is the largest developed artificial lake in Saudi Arabia and is environmentally friendly. It cost about SAR 129 million to build. The total project area is 400,000 square metres, of which the lake covers 210,000 square metres, more than 52% of the total. The lake was created by the Saudi Authority for Industrial Cities and Technology Zones (Modon) in the Second Industrial City in Dammam.

60074552.s: Half Moon Bay is considered one of the most beautiful tourist destinations in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. The beach has clear water and golden sand, making it an ideal place for visitors to enjoy time by the sea.
60074552.b:
Half Moon Bay is considered one of the most beautiful tourist destinations in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. The beach has clear water and golden sand, making it an ideal place for visitors to enjoy time by the sea.

Location

Half Moon Bay is near the city of Khobar, about 30 kilometres from the regional capital, Dammam. It is easy to reach by car, which makes it a favourite destination for many families and tourists.

Activities

Half Moon Bay offers a variety of enjoyable activities, including:

Swimming and sunbathing.

Water sports such as surfing and water skiing.

Short boat trips.

Camping and enjoying the natural surroundings.

Facilities and services

Half Moon Bay has a number of facilities and services that improve the visitor experience, such as:

Restaurants and cafes serving a range of food and drinks.

Designated barbecue areas.

Places to rent items such as umbrellas and chairs.

In short, Half Moon Bay is an ideal destination for anyone who wants to enjoy the sea atmosphere and relax in beautiful natural surroundings. Don't miss the chance to visit this wonderful beach when you visit the Eastern Province!

59938588.t: Al Khalaf and Al Khulaif Village
59938588.s: Al Khalaf and Al Khulaif are two neighbouring village sites only two kilometres apart. Remains of various residential quarters have been found there, along with the remains of the square Al Khalaf Mosque, which covers 324 square metres and shows a fortified character in the height and thickness of its walls and the solidity of its construction. Al Khulaif Mosque has disappeared and nothing remains of it. Both sites contain many graves, as well as inscriptions: 27 have been found, covering an early period of the first Hijri centuries, all in Kufic script that progresses from simple to leafy to floriated.

The two villages are in Qilwah Governorate, part of Al Baha Region, in Tihamah in south-western Saudi Arabia.

59938569.s: Bakhroush bin Allas Al Qurashi Al Zahrani (1170-1230 AH) was a horseman of the Zahran tribe in the Hijaz and a commander of the First Saudi State. After several battles he was killed and beheaded by the invading Ottoman armies led by Muhammad Ali Pasha, the Ottoman governor of Egypt. His castle is one of the most important landmarks of the Kingdom's ancient history, as it tells stories of wars and historical events. It is officially known as the "Bakhroush bin Allas Fortress Village" and lies about 5 km north of Al Atawilah and 37 km from the city of Al Baha.
59938569.b: Bakhroush bin Allas Al Qurashi Al Zahrani (1170-1230 AH) was a horseman of the Zahran tribe in the Hijaz and a commander of the First Saudi State. After several battles he was killed and beheaded by the invading Ottoman armies led by Muhammad Ali Pasha, the Ottoman governor of Egypt. His castle is one of the most important landmarks of the Kingdom's ancient history, as it tells stories of wars and historical events. It is officially known as the "Bakhroush bin Allas Fortress Village" and lies about 5 km north of Al Atawilah and 37 km from the city of Al Baha. The village has several circular forts, designed specifically to reduce the effects of artillery shells. The most notable is Bakhroush Fort, which is distinguished by its large area and its round towers, although part of it has collapsed. The walls were built of tightly packed volcanic stones of varying sizes and colours and coated on the inside with a thick layer of clay, while the roofs were built from tree trunks and branches and then covered with clay. The village also has four mass graves southeast of the castle, for Turkish soldiers who fell in the Battle of Wadi Quraysh in 1229 AH.

59938523.s: Al Atawilah Heritage Village is notable for its high position and its fine views over the Taif-Al Baha regional road and the surrounding areas in every direction. It is roughly 33 km from the city of Al Baha, the regional capital and seat of the emirate. Al Atawilah is generally the largest town in Al Qara Governorate and is the seat of government offices. The village has the Rubu Quraysh Souq, which was held every Thursday and later moved to Wednesday.
59938523.b: Al Atawilah Heritage Village is notable for its high position and its fine views over the Taif-Al Baha regional road and the surrounding areas in every direction. It is roughly 33 km from the city of Al Baha, the regional capital and seat of the emirate. Al Atawilah is generally the largest town in Al Qara Governorate and is the seat of government offices. The village has the Rubu Quraysh Souq, which was held every Thursday and later moved to Wednesday. The souq helped to confirm the village's historical standing: people from the surrounding villages would come to buy, sell and trade in a market governed by inherited laws and customs that acted as covenants regulating trade and dealings between people in the region. Al Atawilah was also distinguished by two defensive forts linked to the village wall, Al Uthman Fort and Dimas Fort. These are buildings of unique stone design with several storeys. In the middle of the village stands the mosque, which still survives today with its unique water systems that were used for ablution.

59938522.s: Daws Museum is a private museum of local heritage in the village of Barhrhah in Al Mandaq Governorate, founded by Bashir Al Zahrani. It holds about 800 heritage and archaeological items, including silverwork, old weapons, farming and kitchen tools, traditional clothing, items made from palm fronds, and old coins. It is licensed by the tourism authority.

59938521.s: Nasser Al Fayyan began collecting heritage items in 1414 AH at his private home in Al Atawilah, Al Baha, and continued his interest in heritage until in 1438 AH he set aside a building for it, in which he gathered thousands of pieces. In 1442 AH the museum was opened to the public. It also has a cafe with seating for families and for young people, and enjoys a lovely view.

59938519.s: Al Safa Historic Mosque stands in the middle of Baljurashi Governorate, about 27 km from the city of Al Baha. It is one of the oldest mosques in the region, more than 1,350 years old, and its door bears the date 46 AH. Its construction is attributed to the Companion Sufyan bin Awf, may God be pleased with him. The mosque was built of local granite stone with juniper-wood columns, and it was included in Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Project for the Development of Historic Mosques, which aims to preserve its authentic architectural character.

59938518.s: Baljurashi Historic Village, also called "Al Malad", is famous for its almonds, grapes, sycamore figs and figs. It is also known for its tall, towering forts on a mountaintop surrounded by old houses. The climate is rainy and cold in winter and mild in summer. The two towers of Al Malad are its best-known historic landmarks.

59938515.s: Humaida Stairs is a historic terraced and paved mountain pass, used in the past by caravans and to carry goods coming down from the Hijaz to Tihamah and going up from it. It was the most important trade route linking Baljurashi with Al Makhwah, Al Qunfudhah on the Red Sea coast, and the cities and towns along the coast.

59938438.s: Mohammed bin Musbeh Museum is housed in a separate building made up of two main halls of 120 square metres each and three rooms of 48 square metres each. The display is varied, using glass display cases and stands to good effect. The museum holds a library of photographs of the Saudi royal family, coins, jewellery and silverware, as well as weapons and war equipment of all kinds, old telephones, traditional clothing, farming and kitchen tools, measures and scales, palm-leaf crafts and copperware. There are also models of a tar-making workshop, a threshing floor, a well and its tools, old doors, and a hand mill.
